You can buy a small bottle of benzoin tincture (got mine on amazon for something like $5) and use some q-tips to wipe it around the area where the adhesive will stick, and it won't come off because of sweat or friction nearly as easily. Benzoin tincture is basically alcohol + some resin from a tree. It's a bit sticky when you first put it on, but it dries quickly and gives the bandage a good surface to stick to.

It's been proven wounds heal MUCH faster if you keep them moist and covered, like with some vaseline and a bandaid. Letting them "air out" will only increase scarring and healing time.

Note but not really an LPT: Many people, doctors included, claim that triple antibiotics don't do anything, although I can tell you the large, deep cut I got on my finger a few weeks ago would have become seriously infected because of the dirty knife I cut it with if I hadn't used triple antibiotic on it for a week or so. Just using bacitracin isn't very likely to reduce dermatitis a lot of people claim to get, as it's by far the most common cause of allergic reactions to topical antibiotics. That said, don't go putting triple antibiotic on every time you get a little cut. Use it if you should be getting stitches but don't have time to or whatever. Otherwise vaseline works just fine to keep wounds moisturized.
